tag: Sprint 14 Task E, F117 (F114 cloud read)

cvar-definition-lower-alpha-tail: Sec. 4, p.4: CVaR defined in Eq. (11) and (12); the limit alpha to 0 giving the minimum and alpha = 1 the expected value is stated in the next paragraph.
prop-5-1-local-minima-not-mapped: Prop. 5.1, Sec. 5, p.5: stated, then shown by an explicit two-qubit example (CVaR_0.5 = sin^2(theta/2), checked) and by the overlap argument for the converse. Short but complete.
cvar-converse-global-minimum-overlap: Sec. 5, p.5: the converse half of the proof of Prop. 5.1. A state with overlap rho on the ground state has CVaR_alpha equal to the minimum for alpha <= rho. Argued with its condition (rho > 0) in the same sentence.
vqe-variational-form-definition: Sec. 2, p.2-3 and Fig. 1: the form is defined (Y-rotations, p repetitions of CZ on all pairs then Y-rotations), with the n(1+p) count, depth O(np) and the nearest-neighbor variant on hardware.
qaoa-parameter-count-vs-vqe: Sec. 3, p.3-4: the QAOA form is defined in Eq. (6) to (9), so 2p parameters follows; the O(n^2 p) rotation and CNOT count is the worst case of the stated construction.
cvar-experiment-setup-six-problems: Sec. 6, p.6: instance sizes, alphas, depths, 340 instances, 14,280 test cases and COBYLA are all stated there (arithmetic checks: 5 x 60 + 4 x 10 = 340).
cvar-simulation-metric-optimal-probabili: Sec. 6.1, p.6: the metric (probability of sampling an optimal solution against iterations divided by qubits, exact simulated state) and the reason for it are stated as the evaluation protocol.
cvar-hardware-ring-layout-setup: Sec. 6.2, p.7 and Fig. 8: qubits 5, 6, 7, 10, 11, 12 in a ring, p = 1, alpha = 10%, 25%, 100%, initial theta = 0, all stated.
cvar-hardware-qaoa-not-used: Sec. 6.2, p.7: the paper states it uses CVaR-VQE and not CVaR-QAOA on hardware and gives its reason, which the value attributes to the authors.
portfolio-instance-parameters-appendix-b: Appendix B, p.11: n = 6, q = 0.5, B = 3, lambda = 12, with the penalty term, and the random mu and sigma are listed.
prop-7-1-proof-induction-loose-bound: Appendix D, p.12-14: the paper does give the proof by induction on p (base case |alpha_0,z| = 1/sqrt(2^n), induction step with three terms) and a lower bound on Delta_p that it calls possibly very loose. This grade covers only what the paper contains, not the correctness of every step.
design-fixes-encoding-and-quantum-subrou: Sec. IV, p.4: the paper fixes problem encoding (random QUBO) and quantum subroutine (BENQO loss) to isolate the classical optimizer, as stated.
random-qubo-instances-negative-diagonal: Sec. IV A, p.4, Eq. (12): off-diagonal entries +U(1,10), diagonal entries -U(1,10), each instance seeded.
noise-model-gaussian-post-processing-fau: Sec. II, p.2 and Sec. IV C, p.6, Eq. (15): Gaussian noise added to exact loss values after simulation, an idealized fault-tolerant scenario.
ansatz-chosen-barren-plateau-free: Sec. II, p.2: the paper states it considers only polynomial-DLA ansatzes with local observables. 'provably barren-plateau-free' is the authors' statement of the property of those choices, cited to prior work.
experiment-size-and-noise-range: Sec. V, p.8: n in [3, 10] and sigma in (1e-3, 1e1), as stated.
repeats-and-ngd-steps: Sec. IV D, p.7: N = 100 repeats with different instances and NGD kmax = 20 steps, as stated.
sigma-star-definition: Sec. VI, p.11: sigma* is defined as the standard deviation of the total loss error beyond which performance falls below 50% of the noise-free level. Note Sec. V (Eq. 27) defines sigma* as the point of steepest descent of the tanh fit; the two agree only when the lower asymptote is near zero.
rae-definition: Sec. VI, Eq. (34), p.11: RAE defined as stated.
approximation-index-definition: Sec. IV E, Eq. (22) and (23), p.7: x_t = 1 if QAR(|psi_max>) >= t, and solvability p_t = (1/N) sum x_t.
limit-noise-model-no-hardware-propagatio: Sec. IV C, p.6: the paper itself says the Gaussian noise model does not explicitly capture hardware-level error propagation.
limit-barren-plateau-ansatzes-untested: Sec. VII D, p.15-16: the paper says it deliberately focused on two barren-plateau-free ansatzes, notes they are efficiently classically simulable, and leaves barren-plateau-prone ansatzes with smart initialization to future work.
vqa-noise-limited-data: Sec. V B, p.10: the paper itself states its data are limited by simulation cost, so scaling conclusions need caution.
vqa-noise-study-setup: Abstract, p.1: states what the study covers (classical optimizers on variational loss functions for random QUBO with Gaussian noise).
controllable-definition: Definition 2 (Sec. II.A, p.3) and Definition 5 (p.4): surjectivity on M, and controllable when controllable on the dynamical Lie group.
barlow-2026-dla-definition: Definition 3, Sec. II.A, p.4, Eq. (16): the span of the Lie closure of the generators.
pauli-basis-dimension: Proposition 2, Sec. II.A, p.3: the basis is stated and the count (4^n strings minus the identity, which is not traceless) is given directly after it. A standard fact with a short complete argument.
controllable-min-parameters: Sec. II.A, p.4, after Definition 5: stated with its reason (Im U = dlg by definition, and Proposition 3, equal dimensions). Proposition 3 is a standard Lie-theory fact stated without proof and the dimension step for a surjective map is not spelled out, so the argument is brief.
simulation-noiseless: Sec. III.A, p.7: 'simulated without shots nor noise', cross entropy loss, Adam optimiser.
hyperparameter-search-design: Sec. III.B, p.7: layers 7 to 25, 100 random trials per set, 100 epochs, top 5 models retrained 250 epochs on a new 1,000-sample set with an 80/20 split.
search-restriction-unverified: Sec. IV.C, p.10: the paper itself calls the restricted-search technique a conjecture and says further experiments are needed to verify it.
subspace-controllable-setup: Sec. III, p.5: 5,000 samples of digits 0, 2 and 6 from MNIST-1D, 10-fold cross validation throughout (decided on the stored value, as the reader left the value empty).
subspace-controllable-single-task: Sec. I, p.2 (repeated in Sec. V): the paper itself says its results are limited to a single classical task.
study-aim: Abstract and Introduction, p.1-2: the paper states it implements two QML models, compares them to classical ones, and analyzes results in an exploratory way.
datasets-sizes: Sec. 1.1, p.2 and Table 1: Bodmas 134,435 files, 57,293 malicious (77,142 benign); PEMachineLearning 201,549 files, 114,737 malicious (86,812 benign). Sums check.
preprocessing-oif: Sec. 1.2, p.3: Ember 2,381 features, 10 chosen by forward selection, plus the import maliciousness score, called OIF.
preprocessing-images: Sec. 1.2, p.3: Grayscale method, 64 x 64 images, called Images; the PCA reduction is used from Sec. 2 on (p.6, Table 5).
qsvm-feature-map-setup: Sec. 2, p.3-5: ZZFeatureMap with d = 2, one circuit per kernel entry, and Pauli, ZZphi and Z feature maps tested (Tables 4 to 6).
qsvm-ibm-limit: Sec. 2, p.7: the paper itself says the hardware test used very small train and test sets because of computation time and queue access, so differences are two or three labels.
qsvm-compute-limit: Sec. 2, p.9: the paper itself says quantum runs need much more computation time on the Qiskit simulator, and it ran smaller datasets or fewer qubits.
qnn-architecture: Sec. 3.1, p.9-10: the algorithm of [8] adapted to two classes; N data qubits plus two ancillas; RY layer then CNOTs; Y, Z, Y rotations on each ancilla; Z expectation; cross entropy with the parameter shift rule.
qnn-first-series-setup: Sec. 3.2, p.10-11: 1000 train and 200 test samples, learning rate 0.1, one epoch, 1 to 3 layers, 4 and 7 data qubits, no varied batch sizes.
qnn-deep-setups: Sec. 3.2, p.11: 4 qubits/5 layers/10 epochs/lr 0.05; 10 layers; 7 qubits/5 layers/5 epochs/lr 0.1; each with a classical equivalent (Tables 14 to 15, 39 to 40, 48 to 49).
overparametrization-def-sec3: Sec. 3.2, p.14: the paper states the term as a reminder in its own words. It is a loose restatement of the concept of [14] and differs from the Fisher-information formulation in Sec. 5; the two are not reconciled.
learning-rate-limit: Sec. 3.2, p.15 and Appendix, p.25: the paper itself says only three learning rates were tested, so no global behavior can be extracted.
spsb-setup: Sec. 4.1, p.16: SPSB estimates gradients in random directions, three circuit passes per input regardless of depth, batch size 32.
reuploading-def: Sec. 4.2, p.18: the paper describes the data reuploading layers (encoding parameters combined with trainable ones in each layer); the method is from [21].
future-work-shots-limit: Sec. 5, p.21: the paper says it does not discuss the shots used for gradient estimates.
malware-exploratory-scope: Introduction p.2 says the work is exploratory. Sec. 3.2, p.12 says the classical NN used batch size 1 in the first series, 'not realistic', and p.13 says batch size 16 was used later. The new value is accurate and more exact than the stored one. Scope and setup statements.
barthe-randomness-source-classical: Sec. II A, p.2: part of the model's own definition (Fig. 1 and the text after Definition 1): randomness is the classical input, support is continuous (Definition 6).
barthe-def-universal-generative-model: Definition 2, Sec. II B, p.2, with the equivalent pointwise CDF form, Eq. (2).
barthe-universality-support-scope: Sec. II B note, p.2: the paper's own choice of support [-1,1]^M and its stated reasons.
barthe-design-summary-product-dense: Sec. VI, p.8 with Sec. III A and III B: the resources of the two designs are fixed by their construction (M qubits with Z observables; n = log(M+1) qubits with observables 2M|m><m| - I, norm 2M - 1). The value does not claim universality.
barthe-dense-construction-appendix-e: Appendix E, p.12: the state, the observables O_m = 2M|m><m| - I, the norm 2M - 1 = Theta(2^n) and <psi|O_m|psi> = Y_m are defined and the identity checks by direct calculation (with Z_m = (Y_m+1)/(2M)). Covers the construction only, not universality.
barthe-appendix-e-abuse-of-notation: Appendix E, p.11: the paper itself says it uses slight abuse of notation in the proof, specifically in the approximations.
barthe-theorem6-proof-spectrum-condition: Appendix F, p.12: condition 1 is shown directly. Lemma 7 gives a state with expectations within epsilon of each vertex, and Tr(O rho) >= lambda_min gives the two eigenvalue bounds. (Typo: c_m = 0 for -1.)
barthe-purification-pure-states: Sec. IV B, p.5: a complete short reduction. A mixed state on n qubits is a pure state on 2n qubits, and a factor 2 does not change an Omega bound. Condition 1 does not depend on the state.
barthe-shadow-tomography-limit: Appendix G, p.13: the paper itself says the result cannot be trivially applied to shadow tomography, with its reason.
barthe-def-primary-mapping: Definition 4, Sec. V A, p.6 with Eq. (7) to (9).
barthe-theorem7-linear-transformation: Theorem 7, Sec. V A, p.6: the proof is the preceding observation that any O equals A P with real A (Pauli expansion) and linearity of expectation.
barthe-lemma3-uncorrelated-variables: Lemma 3, Sec. V A, p.6-7: follows from Theorem 7 by the rank argument given in the text before the lemma (covariance rank limit). The bound 4^n - 1 (identity string is constant) is stated in 'in any case' without explanation.
barthe-regression-generative-transfer-fu: Sec. V B, p.7: the paper says it expects transfer and leaves it for future work.
barthe-no-easy-advantage-path: Sec. VI, p.8: the paper itself says it did not address whether it is a good idea, that advantage is not as easily proven, and that hardness does not connect straightforwardly.
barthe-advantage-left-open: Sec. VI, p.8: stronger advantage arguments are left for future work.

theory_low.cvar-global-optima-coincide-diagonal-rea: Sec. 5, p.5: one sentence, 'the above discussion implies'. No separate proof, and it is an informal consequence (needs the ground-space degeneracy case handled). An authors' consequence, not a stated and proved result.
theory_low.cvar-flat-example-constant-objective: Sec. 5, p.5: only alpha = 0.5 is calculated. The claim for every 0 < alpha < 1 and the 'optimized by decreasing theta' statement rest on Fig. 3, a plotted result, not on a calculation in the text.
theory_low.prop-7-1-qaoa-amplitude-bound: Sec. 7, p.9-10 and Appendix D: the text layer does carry the bound (|alpha_p,z| <= (2^(n+1)(2 - Delta_{p-1} - delta) + 1)^p / sqrt(2^n)) and the proof is given in Appendix D. But the value and quotes drop the bound itself, so the stored record would not carry the result. Re-entered with the formula it could be HIGH (proved result).
theory_low.prop-7-1-flat-state-special-case: Sec. 7, p.10: a discussion of special cases after Prop. 7.1, 'when p = 1 and most diagonal values are equal'. The exact condition (delta >= 1 - 2^(-n(1/2+eps))) is dropped from the value and no separate proof is given. An intuition, not a stated and proved result.
theory_low.qaoa-fixed-depth-flat-risk-limitation: Sec. 7, p.10: 'there is the risk that' is the authors' interpretation of Prop. 7.1 about fixed-depth QAOA in general. It is not a stated limit of their own method.
theory_low.required-shots-grow-exponentially: Sec. VI B, p.12-13: derived from extrapolated fits of sigma*(n) (the paper says none of the three fits is conclusive) combined with a finite-sampling error fit eps_FS (Eq. 37) from n up to 10. A conditional extrapolation of measured results, not a proved result.
theory_low.brute-force-shot-limit-below-nine: Sec. VI B, Eq. (40), p.13: arithmetic from the cited cost criterion of Scriva et al. [18] (n_shots * n_calls < 2^n) and an assumed cost model (20 NGD steps, 1 + 2n calls). 2^n / (20(1+2n)) is below 1 for n <= 8, so the arithmetic checks, but the 'impossible' claim rests on that cited criterion and brute force as the only classical baseline.
theory_low.exponential-boundary-quantum-advantage-u: Sec. VI B, Fig. 11, p.13: the authors say it 'strongly suggests'. An interpretation of an extrapolated curve under an assumed exponential decay of sigma*.
theory_low.power-law-log-boundary-small-window: Sec. VI B, Fig. 11, p.13: read off extrapolated curves (n >= 20 and n >= 25); the authors say the advantages are only theoretical. A result from extrapolated fits.
theory_low.runtime-lower-bound-exceeds-one-hour: Sec. VI B, Eq. (41), p.14: uses the cited runtime bound of [18], extrapolated shot counts and assumed D = O(1) and t_gate = 100 ns. An estimate, not a result the paper proves.
theory_low.vqe-shot-extrapolation-lower-resources: Sec. VII B, Fig. 13, p.14: a power-law fit to simulated data for n up to 13, extrapolated to n >= 243. A measured and extrapolated result.
theory_low.hea-mostly-uncontrollable-nisq: Sec. II.B, p.4: 'most HEA circuits in the NISQ era are uncontrollable' is a general claim with no derivation. The figure 228 is arithmetic (4095 / 18 = 227.5, rounded up) of a necessary parameter count only.
theory_low.barthe-appendix-a-triangular-map: Appendix A, p.9-10: the paper gives 'intuition' and says the map is 'the essence of triangular mapping in [BKM05]'. Lemma 1 is the cited result and the boundedness and piecewise continuity get a one-line reason. A cited result and a sketch.
theory_low.barthe-theorem1-pointwise-density-suffic: Sec. II C, p.3: the substance is the cited sufficient condition from [KPB21]. The paper adds only the inclusion of monotone functions in all functions. A result proved elsewhere and cited.
theory_low.barthe-theorem2-product-pointwise-densit: Sec. III A, p.3 and Appendices B and C: rests on the cited one-qubit universality Theorem 9 of [PSLNGS+21] and the cited Baire class 1 result. The multivariate step is one sentence ('stacking M universal circuits'). Theorem 11's proof is thin (see that item).
theory_low.barthe-theorem3-product-encoding-univers: Sec. III A, p.3-4: deduced in prose from Theorems 1 and 2 ('This yields...'). Theorem 1 asks density in ALL functions, while Theorem 2 gives density only in bounded piecewise continuous ones, and the step to the Wasserstein epsilon is not written out. No proof is given beyond the chain.
theory_low.barthe-first-central-result-constant-nor: Sec. III A, p.4: the summary sentence of Theorem 3, so it carries the same gaps (prose-level chain through Theorems 1 and 2, cited universality).
theory_low.barthe-infinite-support-extension: Appendix D, p.11: a short note. It defines a truncating sequence and says it converges in distribution. It does not say how the observable norm must scale, and the claim about finite moments is not shown.
theory_low.barthe-theorem4-dense-encoding-universal: Sec. III B and Appendix E, p.11-12: a construction sketch. It uses a cited state-preparation architecture [PB11] and a cited one-qubit approximation, the approximations are marked 'slight abuse of notation', and the approximate-equality notation is never defined. The Wasserstein epsilon is not derived.
theory_low.barthe-lemma4-pure-state-circuit: Appendix E, p.11: holds by the cited architecture [PB11] and a mapping g that is only asserted to exist. A short argument that relies on cited work.
theory_low.barthe-lemma5-lemma6-approximate-rz: Appendix E, p.12: Lemma 5 is taken from the proof in [PSLNGS+21] (cited) and the approximation symbol is not defined. Lemma 6 follows in one line with no error analysis.
theory_low.barthe-theorem5-dimension-bound: Sec. IV A, p.4-5: argued informally. A single-qubit example, then 'Extending this reasoning to several qubits, we find...'. No proof is given that M > 4^n - 1 rules out approximation for all epsilon.
theory_low.barthe-theorem6-holevo-necessary-conditi: cross-group consistency, Rule A (coordinator, 2026-10-30): Theorem 6, Sec. IV B, p.5; proof App. F, pp.12-13: condition 2 rests on 'Holevo's bound (found as Theorem 5.1 in [ANTSV02])', Eq. (F3), the Ambainis-Nayak-Ta-Shma-Vazirani random-access-code bound nL >= (1 - H(q))M, cited and not proved. The proof also says it combines approaches from Theorem 2.6 in [Aar07] and B.1 in [JGM+23]. Chernoff is background; the [ANTSV02] bound is a specific cited result.
theory_low.barthe-theorem6-final-inequality-and-spe: cross-group consistency, Rule A (coordinator, 2026-10-30): App. F, p.13, Eqs. (F3)-(F7): the final inequality combines Chernoff (background) with Eq. (F3), Theorem 5.1 of [ANTSV02], cited and not proved. The comparison with [JGM+23] follows from Lambda <= ||O||^2, but the inequality itself rests on the cited bound.
theory_low.barthe-corollary1-product-optimal: cross-group consistency, Rule A (coordinator, 2026-10-30): Corollary 1, Sec. IV C, p.5: optimality is measured against n in Omega(M/||O||^2) from Theorem 6, condition 2, which rests on Theorem 5.1 of [ANTSV02], cited and not proved (App. F, p.13, Eq. (F3)). Transitive on barthe-theorem6-holevo-necessary-conditions.
theory_low.barthe-corollary2-dense-gap: cross-group consistency, Rule A (coordinator, 2026-10-30): Corollary 2, Sec. IV C, p.5: the gap uses n >= log4(M+1) from Theorem 5, which the paper argues informally ('Extending this reasoning to several qubits, we find', p.4-5; barthe-theorem5-dimension-bound is graded low), and the Omega bound from Theorem 6, which rests on Theorem 5.1 of [ANTSV02] (App. F, p.13). Both inputs are unproved here.
theory_low.barthe-lemma2-measurement-count: Sec. IV D and Appendix G, p.13: proved only under an assumed independent Gaussian shot-noise model. Also epsilon^2 in Theta(||O||/t) is stated without derivation, while a measurement of an observable with norm ||O|| has variance of order ||O||^2/t, so the exponent on ||O|| in Eq. (6) looks wrong.
theory_low.barthe-appendix-g-gaussian-shot-noise-mo: Appendix G, p.13: the value joins the stated simplifying assumption with the authors' claim that epsilon^2 is in Theta(||O||/t), which is not derived (the variance of a norm-||O|| observable is of order ||O||^2/t) and relies on a cited lemma [AGS05].
theory_low.barthe-tradeoff-qubits-measurements: Sec. IV C and IV D, p.5-6: the trade-off rests on Lemma 2 (simplified noise model) and is called a 'hint' and 'highlights' in the text. Authors' interpretation.
theory_low.barthe-theorem8-finite-chaos-expansion: Sec. V B, p.7: no proof. It extends the cited finite-Fourier-series fact of [SSM21] in one sentence.
theory_low.barthe-theorem10-expectation-universalit: cross-group consistency, Rule A (coordinator, 2026-10-30): Theorem 10, App. B, p.10: proved from 'Theorem 4 from [PSLNGS+21]', restated as Theorem 9 and cited, not proved. The universality rests on that cited result; the review's own why already notes the team lead may prefer low.
theory_low.barthe-theorem11-pointwise-density: Appendix C, p.10-11: one sentence, 'building on Theorem 10'. The pointwise-limit step rests on the cited Baire class 1 results [Lac84, Leb04] and no argument is written out.
theory_low.barthe-necessary-conditions-tradeoff: The reader's value is more exact than the stored one: it names the Gaussian shot-noise assumption and the gap. Stored value overstates ('show a trade-off'). The measurement side rests on Lemma 2 under a simplified noise model, and Theorem 5 is argued informally; the authors' trade-off is an interpretation. Set LOW at the team lead's decision, 2026-10-31 (Sprint 14 Manual Validation Q1 option 1).
theory_low.barthe-universality-proved: The new value is the more exact one (names the two designs and the epsilon-Wasserstein form). But Theorems 3 and 4 are prose-level chains or sketches that rest on cited results (Theorem 9, Baire class 1, [PB11]); Theorem 1 asks density in all functions and Theorem 2 gives it only for piecewise continuous ones. The paper does claim and construct these, so as a statement of what the paper claims it is right, but the proofs do not settle it. Set LOW at the team lead's decision, 2026-10-31 (Sprint 14 Manual Validation Q1 option 1).
